label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Descriptive Statistics & Probability Axioms
label.ar: ● Level 1 Foundation — Descriptive الإحصاء & الاحتمال Axioms

body.en:
Measures of Central Tendency & Dispersion:

  • Mean (from frequency distribution): \[ \bar{x} = \frac{\sum f_i x_i}{\sum f_i} = \frac{\sum f_i x_i}{n}. \]
  • Variance & Standard Deviation: \[ \sigma^2 = \frac{\sum f_i (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n} = \frac{\sum f_i x_i^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2, \quad \sigma = \sqrt{\sigma^2}. \]
  • Interquartile Range & Outliers: \(IQR = Q_3 - Q_1\). A data value \(x\) is an outlier if: \[ x < Q_1 - 1.5 \times IQR \quad \text{or} \quad x > Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR. \]

Combinatorics & Probability Laws:

  • Permutations (Order Matters): \({}^n P_r = \frac{n!}{(n - r)!}\).
  • Combinations (Order Does Not Matter): \({}^n C_r = \binom{n}{r} = \frac{n!}{r!(n - r)!}\).
  • Addition Rule: \[ P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B). \] For mutually exclusive events, \(P(A \cap B) = 0 \implies P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B)\).
  • Conditional Probability: \[ P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} \iff P(A \cap B) = P(B)P(A \mid B). \]
  • Independence Criterion: Events \(A\) and \(B\) are independent if and only if \(P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)\), which is equivalent to \(P(A \mid B) = P(A)\).

label.en: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Binomial & Normal Distributions
label.ar: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Binomial & Normal Distributions (الموضوع ٤ · الإحصاء والاحتمالات والتوزيعات)

body.en:
Discrete Random Variable \(X\): A mapping from the sample space to \(\mathbb{R}\) with probability mass function \(P(X = x)\) satisfying \(0 \le P(X = x) \le 1\) and \(\sum P(X = x) = 1\). Expected value (mean) and variance:

\[ E(X) = \mu = \sum x P(X = x), \quad \text{Var}(X) = \sigma^2 = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2 = \sum x^2 P(X = x) - \mu^2. \]

Binomial Distribution \(X \sim B(n, p)\): Models the number of successes in \(n\) independent Bernoulli trials each having constant success probability \(p\):

\[ P(X = k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1 - p)^{n - k} \quad \text{for } k = 0, 1, 2, \dots, n. \]

Key parameters: \[ E(X) = np, \quad \text{Var}(X) = np(1 - p), \quad \sigma = \sqrt{np(1 - p)}. \]

Continuous Normal Distribution \(X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)\): Characterised by the bell-shaped density curve symmetric about \(\mu\), with points of inflection at \(x = \mu \pm \sigma\). The standardised variable is:

\[ Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} \sim N(0, 1). \]

Any probability \(P(a \le X \le b)\) equals \(P\left(\frac{a - \mu}{\sigma} \le Z \le \frac{b - \mu}{\sigma}\right)\). Symmetry identities: \(P(Z < -z) = P(Z > z) = 1 - P(Z < z)\).
body.ar:
Discrete Random المتغير \(X\): A mapping from the sample space to \(\mathbb{R}\) with الاحتمال mass الدالة \(P(X = x)\) satisfying \(0 \le P(X = x) \le 1\) and \(\sum P(X = x) = 1\). Expected value (mean) and variance:

\[ E(X) = \mu = \sum x P(X = x), \quad \text{Var}(X) = \sigma^2 = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2 = \sum x^2 P(X = x) - \mu^2. \]

Binomial Distribution \(X \sim B(n, p)\): Models the number of successes in \(n\) independent Bernoulli trials each having الثابت success الاحتمال \(p\):

\[ P(X = k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1 - p)^{n - k} \quad \text{for } k = 0, 1, 2, \dots, n. \]

Key المعاملات: \[ E(X) = np, \quad \text{Var}(X) = np(1 - p), \quad \sigma = \sqrt{np(1 - p)}. \]

Continuous التوزيع الطبيعي \(X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)\): Characterised by the bell-shaped density curve symmetric about \(\mu\), with points of inflection at \(x = \mu \pm \sigma\). The standardised المتغير is:

\[ Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} \sim N(0, 1). \]

Any الاحتمال \(P(a \le X \le b)\) equals \(P\left(\frac{a - \mu}{\sigma} \le Z \le \frac{b - \mu}{\sigma}\right)\). Symmetry المتطابقات: \(P(Z < -z) = P(Z > z) = 1 - P(Z < z)\).

label.en: ● Level 3 University Rigor — Bivariate Data, Pearson \(r\) & Regression Invariants
label.ar: ● Level 3 University Rigor — Bivariate Data, Pearson \(r\) & Regression Invariants (الموضوع ٤ · الإحصاء والاحتمالات والتوزيعات)

body.en:
Pearson's Product-Moment Correlation Coefficient \(r\): Measures the strength and direction of linear association between paired variables \((x_i, y_i)\):

\[ r = \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})(y_i - \bar{y})}{\sqrt{\sum(x_i - \bar{x})^2 \sum(y_i - \bar{y})^2}} = \frac{s_{xy}}{s_x s_y}, \quad -1 \le r \le 1. \]

The coefficient of determination \(r^2\) represents the proportion of total variation in \(y\) explained by the linear relationship with \(x\).

Least Squares Regression Line (LSRL) of \(y\) on \(x\): \[ \hat{y} = mx + c, \quad \text{where } m = \frac{s_{xy}}{s_x^2} = r\frac{s_y}{s_x}. \]

Theorem (Mean Center Invariant): The least-squares regression line of \(y\) on \(x\) must pass through the mean point \((\bar{x}, \bar{y})\). That is, \(\bar{y} = m\bar{x} + c\).

Reliability Guidelines: Predictions made within the range of observed \(x\)-values (interpolation) are reliable if \(|r|\) is sufficiently close to 1. Predictions outside the observed range (extrapolation) are inherently hazardous because the linear trend cannot be assumed to persist indefinitely. Never use the regression line of \(y\) on \(x\) to estimate \(x\) from \(y\) (the line of \(x\) on \(y\) is required for that purpose).
body.ar:
Pearson's Product-Moment Correlation المعامل \(r\): Measures the strength and direction of linear association between paired المتغيرات \((x_i, y_i)\):

\[ r = \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})(y_i - \bar{y})}{\sqrt{\sum(x_i - \bar{x})^2 \sum(y_i - \bar{y})^2}} = \frac{s_{xy}}{s_x s_y}, \quad -1 \le r \le 1. \]

The المعامل of determination \(r^2\) represents the proportion of total variation in \(y\) explained by the linear relationship with \(x\).

Least Squares Regression Line (LSRL) of \(y\) on \(x\): \[ \hat{y} = mx + c, \quad \text{where } m = \frac{s_{xy}}{s_x^2} = r\frac{s_y}{s_x}. \]

Theorem (Mean Center Invariant): The least-squares regression line of \(y\) on \(x\) must pass through the mean point \((\bar{x}, \bar{y})\). That is, \(\bar{y} = m\bar{x} + c\).

Predictions outside the observed المدى (extrapolation) are inherently hazardous because the linear trend cannot be assumed to persist indefinitely. body.en:
Why Bayes' Theorem & Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion Work: Any event \(B\) can be partitioned into disjoint intersections \(B = (B \cap A) \cup (B \cap A')\). By additivity of mutually exclusive events and the multiplication rule \(P(A \cap B) = P(B \mid A)P(A)\):

\[ P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} = \frac{P(B \mid A)P(A)}{P(B \mid A)P(A) + P(B \mid A')P(A')} \]

Similarly, in counting \(|A \cup B|\), summing \(|A| + |B|\) counts every element in \(A \cap B\) twice; subtracting \(|A \cap B|\) once restores exact cardinality: \(P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)\).
body.ar:
Why Bayes' مبرهنة & Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion Work: Any event \(B\) can be partitioned into disjoint intersections \(B = (B \cap A) \cup (B \cap A')\). By additivity of mutually exclusive events and the multiplication rule \(P(A \cap B) = P(B \mid A)P(A)\):

\[ P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} = \frac{P(B \mid A)P(A)}{P(B \mid A)P(A) + P(B \mid A')P(A')} \]

Similarly, in counting \(|A \cup B|\), summing \(|A| + |B|\) counts every element in \(A \cap B\) twice; subtracting \(|A \cap B|\) once restores exact cardinality: \(P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)\).

label.en: Worked Example 4.1 — Permutations & Combinations in Probability
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.1 — Permutations & Combinations in الاحتمال

problem.en:
A committee of 5 is to be chosen at random from a group of 6 teachers and 8 students.
(a) Find the total number of different committees that can be formed.
(b) Find the probability that the committee contains exactly 2 teachers and 3 students.
(c) Find the probability that the committee contains at least 3 teachers.
problem.ar:
A committee of 5 is to be chosen at random from a group of 6 teachers and 8 students.
(a) أوجد total number of different committees that can be formed.
(b) أوجد احتمال that the committee contains exactly 2 teachers and 3 students.
(c) أوجد احتمال that the committee contains at least 3 teachers.

solution.en:
(a) Total members = \(6 + 8 = 14\). Since order does not matter:
\[ \text{Total committees} = \binom{14}{5} = \frac{14!}{5! \, 9!} = \frac{14 \times 13 \times 12 \times 11 \times 10}{5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 2002. \]

(b) Number of favorable committees with 2 teachers and 3 students:
\[ N = \binom{6}{2} \times \binom{8}{3} = 15 \times 56 = 840. \]
\[ P(\text{2 teachers, 3 students}) = \frac{840}{2002} = \frac{60}{143} \approx 0.4196. \]

(c) "At least 3 teachers" means 3, 4, or 5 teachers:
\[ N_3 = \binom{6}{3}\binom{8}{2} = 20 \times 28 = 560. \]
\[ N_4 = \binom{6}{4}\binom{8}{1} = 15 \times 8 = 120. \]
\[ N_5 = \binom{6}{5}\binom{8}{0} = 6 \times 1 = 6. \]
Total favorable = \(560 + 120 + 6 = 686\).
\[ P(\text{at least 3 teachers}) = \frac{686}{2002} = \frac{49}{143} \approx 0.3427. \]
solution.ar:
خطوات الحل:

(a) Total members = \(6 + 8 = 14\). Since order does not matter:
\[ \text{Total committees} = \binom{14}{5} = \frac{14!}{5! \, 9!} = \frac{14 \times 13 \times 12 \times 11 \times 10}{5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 2002. \]

(b) Number of favorable committees with 2 teachers and 3 students:
\[ N = \binom{6}{2} \times \binom{8}{3} = 15 \times 56 = 840. \]
\[ P(\text{2 teachers, 3 students}) = \frac{840}{2002} = \frac{60}{143} \approx 0.4196. \]

(c) "At least 3 teachers" means 3, 4, or 5 teachers:
\[ N_3 = \binom{6}{3}\binom{8}{2} = 20 \times 28 = 560. \]
\[ N_4 = \binom{6}{4}\binom{8}{1} = 15 \times 8 = 120. \]
\[ N_5 = \binom{6}{5}\binom{8}{0} = 6 \times 1 = 6. \]
Total favorable = \(560 + 120 + 6 = 686\).
\[ P(\text{at least 3 teachers}) = \frac{686}{2002} = \frac{49}{143} \approx 0.3427. \]

label.ar: مثال محلول 4.2 — التوزيع الطبيعي Unknown المعاملات

problem.en: The mass \(X\) of adult apples produced in an orchard is normally distributed with mean \(\mu\) and standard deviation \(\sigma\). Given that \(P(X < 140) = 0.08\) and \(P(X > 210) = 0.05\), find the exact values of \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\) to three significant figures.
problem.ar: The mass \(X\) of adult apples produced in an orchard is normally distributed with mean \(\mu\) and الانحراف المعياري \(\sigma\). بما أن \(P(X < 140) = 0.08\) and \(P(X > 210) = 0.05\), أوجد exact values of \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\) to three significant figures.

solution.en:
1. Convert given probabilities to standard normal \(Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}\):
\(P(X < 140) = 0.08 \implies P(Z < z_1) = 0.08\).
Using GDC `invNorm(0.08, 0, 1)`: \[ z_1 = -1.4051. \]
For the upper tail: \(P(X > 210) = 0.05 \implies P(X < 210) = 0.95 \implies P(Z < z_2) = 0.95\).
Using GDC `invNorm(0.95, 0, 1)`: \[ z_2 = 1.6449. \]

2. Form a system of linear equations in \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\):
\[ \frac{140 - \mu}{\sigma} = -1.4051 \implies 140 - \mu = -1.4051\sigma \implies \mu - 1.4051\sigma = 140. \]
\[ \frac{210 - \mu}{\sigma} = 1.6449 \implies 210 - \mu = 1.6449\sigma \implies \mu + 1.6449\sigma = 210. \]

3. Subtract the first equation from the second:
\[ (1.6449 - (-1.4051))\sigma = 210 - 140 \implies 3.0500\sigma = 70 \implies \sigma = \frac{70}{3.0500} \approx 22.95 \approx 23.0\text{ g}. \]

4. Substitute \(\sigma\) back to determine \(\mu\):
\[ \mu = 210 - 1.6449(22.951) = 210 - 37.752 \approx 172.25 \approx 172\text{ g}. \]

Conclusion: \(\mu = 172\text{ g}\) and \(\sigma = 23.0\text{ g}\) (to 3 s.f.).
solution.ar:
1. Convert المعطيات probabilities to standard normal \(Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}\):
\(P(X < 140) = 0.08 \implies P(Z < z_1) = 0.08\).
Using GDC `invNorm(0.08, 0, 1)`: \[ z_1 = -1.4051. \]
For the upper tail: \(P(X > 210) = 0.05 \implies P(X < 210) = 0.95 \implies P(Z < z_2) = 0.95\).
Using GDC `invNorm(0.95, 0, 1)`: \[ z_2 = 1.6449. \]

2. Form a system of المعادلات الخطية in \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\):
\[ \frac{140 - \mu}{\sigma} = -1.4051 \implies 140 - \mu = -1.4051\sigma \implies \mu - 1.4051\sigma = 140. \]
\[ \frac{210 - \mu}{\sigma} = 1.6449 \implies 210 - \mu = 1.6449\sigma \implies \mu + 1.6449\sigma = 210. \]

3. Subtract the first المعادلة from the second:
\[ (1.6449 - (-1.4051))\sigma = 210 - 140 \implies 3.0500\sigma = 70 \implies \sigma = \frac{70}{3.0500} \approx 22.95 \approx 23.0\text{ g}. \]

4. عوّض \(\sigma\) back to determine \(\mu\):
\[ \mu = 210 - 1.6449(22.951) = 210 - 37.752 \approx 172.25 \approx 172\text{ g}. \]

Conclusion: \(\mu = 172\text{ g}\) and \(\sigma = 23.0\text{ g}\) (to 3 s.f.).

body.en:
Binomial Strict vs Inclusive Inequalities: Because \(X\) is discrete, \(P(X \ge 5) = 1 - P(X \le 4)\), NOT \(1 - P(X \le 5)\). Similarly, \(P(X > 5) = 1 - P(X \le 5)\). Always sketch a quick number line for discrete sums.

Negative Z-scores: When finding unknown \(\mu\) or \(\sigma\) from a lower tail probability \(< 0.5\), remember that \(z\) must be negative. Omitting the minus sign creates non-physical negative standard deviations.

Regression Directionality: The regression line of \(y\) on \(x\) can ONLY be used to predict \(y\) from \(x\). Rearranging \(\hat{y} = mx + c\) algebraically to solve for \(x\) given \(y\) violates least-squares minimization and earns 0 marks on Paper 2.
body.ar:
Binomial Strict vs Inclusive المتباينات: Because \(X\) is discrete, \(P(X \ge 5) = 1 - P(X \le 4)\), NOT \(1 - P(X \le 5)\). Similarly, \(P(X > 5) = 1 - P(X \le 5)\). Always sketch a quick number line for discrete sums.

Negative Z-scores: عندما finding unknown \(\mu\) or \(\sigma\) from a lower tail الاحتمال \(< 0.5\), remember that \(z\) must be negative. Omitting the minus sign creates non-physical negative standard deviations.

Regression Directionality: The regression line of \(y\) on \(x\) can ONLY be used to predict \(y\) from \(x\). Rearranging \(\hat{y} = mx + c\) algebraically to أوجد قيمة \(x\) المعطيات \(y\) violates least-squares minimization and earns 0 marks on Paper 2.

The masses of apples from an orchard follow \(M \sim \text{N}(180, \sigma^2)\) grams. Given that \(15\%\) of apples have mass greater than \(195\text{ g}\):

(b) Twelve apples are chosen at random. Find the probability that at least three of them have a mass greater than \(195\text{ g}\). [4]

\(P(Y \ge 3) = 1 - P(Y \le 2) = 1 - \text{binomcdf}(12, 0.15, 2)\) [M1]
\(= 1 - 0.7358 = 0.264\) (3 s.f.) [A1] [A1]

question.en:
Practice 4.1: A multiple-choice examination consists of 20 independent questions, each having 4 options of which only one is correct. A student guesses randomly on all questions. Let \(X\) be the number of correct answers.
(a) State the distribution of \(X\) including its parameters.
(b) Find the probability that the student passes by scoring at least 10 correct answers.
(c) Calculate the mean and standard deviation of \(X\).
question.ar:
Practice 4.1: A multiple-choice examination consists of 20 independent questions, each having 4 options of which only one is correct. A student guesses randomly on all questions. ليكن \(X\) be the number of correct answers.
(a) State the distribution of \(X\) including its parameters.
(b) أوجد احتمال أن the student passes by scoring at least 10 correct answers.
(c) احسب mean and standard deviation of \(X\).

solution.en:
(a) \(X \sim B(n, p)\) with \(n = 20\) and \(p = 0.25\).
(b) \(P(X \ge 10) = 1 - P(X \le 9)\).
Using GDC `binomcdf(20, 0.25, 9)`: \(P(X \le 9) \approx 0.9861\).
\[ P(X \ge 10) = 1 - 0.9861 = 0.0139 \quad (1.39\%). \]
(c) Mean: \(\mu = np = 20 \times 0.25 = 5\).
Standard deviation: \(\sigma = \sqrt{np(1 - p)} = \sqrt{20 \times 0.25 \times 0.75} = \sqrt{3.75} \approx 1.936 \approx 1.94\).

question.en:
Practice 4.2: Bivariate data for study hours \(x\) and exam mark \(y\) across 10 students yield \(\bar{x} = 14.5\), \(\bar{y} = 72.0\), and Pearson's correlation coefficient \(r = 0.88\). The regression line of \(y\) on \(x\) has equation \(y = 2.4x + c\).
(a) Find the value of \(c\).
(b) Interpret the slope \(2.4\) in context.
(c) Estimate the exam mark of a student who studies 18 hours.
question.ar:
Practice 4.2: Bivariate data for study hours \(x\) and exam mark \(y\) across 10 students yield \(\bar{x} = 14.5\), \(\bar{y} = 72.0\), and Pearson's correlation coefficient \(r = 0.88\). The regression line of \(y\) on \(x\) has equation \(y = 2.4x + c\).
(a) أوجد قيمة \(c\).
(b) Interpret the slope \(2.4\) in context.
(c) Estimate the exam mark of a student who studies 18 hours.

solution.en:
(a) The regression line must pass through the mean point \((\bar{x}, \bar{y}) = (14.5, 72.0)\):
\[ 72.0 = 2.4(14.5) + c \implies 72.0 = 34.8 + c \implies c = 72.0 - 34.8 = 37.2. \]
Thus \(y = 2.4x + 37.2\).

(b) The slope \(2.4\) indicates that for each additional hour of study, a student's predicted exam mark increases by 2.4 marks.

(c) For \(x = 18\):
\[ \hat{y} = 2.4(18) + 37.2 = 43.2 + 37.2 = 80.4\text{ marks}. \]
